chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:

I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام: A man came to a man. He said: "If he is muhsan, then upon him is execution; and if he is not muhsan, then upon him is flogging." He said: So I said: Then what is upon the one to whom it was done? He said: "Upon him is execution in every case, whether he was muhsan or not muhsan."

key_terms.الْجَلْدُ: flogging as the prescribed punishment for the non-muhsan party
key_terms.الْقَتْلُ: execution as the prescribed hadd punishment in this context
key_terms.الْمُؤْتَى: the one to whom the act was done, i.e., the passive party in the case described
key_terms.عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ: in every circumstance, without distinction in the stated ruling
key_terms.مُحْصَنًا: legally protected through prior marriage, affecting the legal punishment

ai.seo_question: What punishment does this hadith assign in a case of لِوَاط according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Imam Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام concerning the prescribed punishment in a case of liwat. It distinguishes between the active party based on ihsan status, while stating that the passive party is subject to execution in all cases.
